s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin lesions with systemic involvement
salient_findings: Purpura and ecchymoses with progression over 12 months
Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in multiple regions
Abnormal liver function test results and renal impairment
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss
Medical history of alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment
Purpura and ecchymoses initially periorbital, progressed over 12 months
Elder abuse excluded
Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results
Unremarkable radiological studies
Hematoxylin-eosin staining showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits
Congo red staining results were positive
Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence

shortlist.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy, consistent with amyloid deposits

shortlist.label: Lipoid proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura, consistent with clinical presentation of lipoid proteinosis

shortlist.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic involvement with anemia, abnormal liver function, and renal impairment, which can be associated with secondary amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Familial amyloid polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Amyloid deposits on biopsy, although less likely given the absence of prominent neuropathic symptoms

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpura and ecchymoses with systemic involvement, although less common than amyloidosis

rule_in.why: it is more common in older adults

rule_out.why: age and sex are not specific to any candidate

trace.fact: Chief complaint: purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss

rule_in.why: it commonly presents with purpura and weight loss

rule_out.why: it does not typically present with purpura or ecchymoses

rule_in.why: the time course is not specific enough

rule_out.why: it does not discriminate between the candidates

rule_in.why: it often presents with periorbital lesions

rule_out.why: lesion location is not specific enough

trace.fact: Lesion progression: progressed over the previous 12 months

rule_in.why: it does not discriminate between the candidates
alcohol abuse is a risk factor

rule_out.why: alcohol abuse is more commonly associated with other conditions

rule_in.why: cognitive impairment is not specific to any candidate

rule_out.why: cognitive impairment is not specific to rule out any candidate
